Editor's review pack

For Dr Kunda Shahane, editor-in-chief. Everything that needs her decision or signature is in this one document.

Each claim appears once, even if several units use it. Claims she has already verified are not repeated.

Claims that a second AI has not yet confirmed against the source are held back, so that she checks each fact only once.

4 decision(s). 5 claim(s) to approve again. 424 new claim(s) to check. 14 claim(s) held back until cross-checked.

Part A. Decisions

Q1. ASE guideline, pulsed-wave Doppler of the aortic arch and isthmus. The text (p. 689) includes 'arches' in the minimum assessment; Table 6 (p. 693) marks the transverse arch and isthmus optional and separately requires the distal ductus arteriosus. ChatGPT's check of the PDF confirmed that the guideline does not reconcile the two. How should the course teach it?

☐ Teach as optional (as in Table 6)

☐ Teach as required (as in the text)

☐ Keep the present wording: state both, teach neither as the rule

If no answer: Present wording stays: units F1 and XA5 state the disagreement and teach neither reading as the rule.

Affects: Units F1 and XA5

Q2. After a normal early (11 to 14 week) heart check, may unit D9 say plainly that the full second-trimester cardiac screen is still required? The ASE guideline says this for early fetal echocardiography (repeat at 18 to 20 weeks); the ISUOG screening guideline does not say it in so many words.

☐ Yes, say it plainly for screening as the editor's teaching

☐ No, keep it as the ASE statement about echocardiography only

If no answer: D9 quotes the ASE statement under its own heading and makes no rule for screening.

Affects: Unit D9

Q3. Rate thresholds. ISUOG (screening): refer for a persistent rate of 110 or less, or 180 or more. ASE (echocardiography): a sustained rate below 120, or above 160 to 180, is abnormal. Units D8 and F2 teach the ISUOG thresholds for the screener and mention the ASE wording. Is that right for this course?

☐ Yes

☐ No, teach this instead: ____________

If no answer: As drafted: ISUOG thresholds for the screener, ASE wording mentioned.

Affects: Units D8, D10, F2

Q4. Does the consent held for archive cases cover publication for teaching in a paid product (not only clinical care)?

☐ Yes, wording covers it

☐ No or unsure: re-consent or do not use

☐ Ask the legal advisor

If no answer: No archive clip is published until this is confirmed in writing.

Affects: All clip drills and the case atlas

IS23-017Still frames and video clips of the recommended structures and views should be archived so that the examination can later be reviewed for adequacy, with appropriate patient identification in the clinical examination record, labelling of laterality and orientation where appropriate, and consideration of local or national archiving standards (good practice point). Note: Approved by the editor on 13 Nov 2026 in an earlier wording (Dr Kunda Shahane, 2026-11-13 (approved review sheet for v0.2 in full; approval relayed by the project owner)). Reworded after the cross-check found: Technical factors, Zoom, cine-loop and image storage, p. 789 also calls for appropriate patient identification in the clinical examination record and consideration of local or national archiving standards. Laterality and orientation labels alone do not cover its documentation instructions. Needs the editor's re-approval.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Technical factors: Zoom, cine-loop and image storage, p. 789D1, D2, D3, D5, D6, D13
IS23-036Transient bradycardia is seen in normal second-trimester fetuses and is associated with transducer pressure; persistent bradycardia (110 bpm or less) in a well fetus needs timely evaluation by a fetal cardiac specialist. Possible causes include frequent blocked atrial ectopic beats, atrioventricular block and sinus bradycardia. Note: Approved by the editor on 13 Nov 2026 in an earlier wording (Dr Kunda Shahane, 2026-11-13 (approved review sheet for v0.2 in full; approval relayed by the project owner)). Reworded after the cross-check found: Four-chamber view, p. 792 describes an association between transient bradycardia and probe pressure. “Often from” strengthens that association to a cause. The persistent rate threshold, well-fetus qualifier, referral and listed possible causes agree. Needs the editor's re-approval.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Four-chamber view, p. 792D1, D8, D10, F2
IS23-047Two separate atrioventricular valves should open separately and freely, with the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve inserting closer to the apex than the mitral valve (normal offset); abnormal alignment can be a key sonographic finding in anomalies such as atrioventricular septal defect. Note: Approved by the editor on 13 Nov 2026 in an earlier wording (Dr Kunda Shahane, 2026-11-13 (approved review sheet for v0.2 in full; approval relayed by the project owner)). Reworded after the cross-check found: Four-chamber view, p. 793 says abnormal AV valve alignment can be a key sonographic finding in anomalies such as AV septal defect. The claim makes it categorical. The normal offset and valve-opening descriptions agree. Needs the editor's re-approval.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Four-chamber view, p. 793; Table 1D1, D4, D13
IS23-063The axial appearances of the RVOT, branch pulmonary arteries and ductal and aortic arches form a continuum of views that varies with transducer orientation and fetal lie; assessment is likely to be more reliable live or on cine-loop than from still images alone. Note: Approved by the editor on 13 Nov 2026 in an earlier wording (Dr Kunda Shahane, 2026-11-13 (approved review sheet for v0.2 in full; approval relayed by the project owner)). Reworded after the cross-check found: RVOT view, 3VV and 3VTV, p. 794 describes greater reliability of live or cine review as likely. The claim states it without that qualification. Figure 8 on p. 795 illustrates the continuum. Needs the editor's re-approval.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: RVOT view, 3VV and 3VTV, p. 794; Figure 8, p. 795D1, D6, D13
IS23-077In routine second-trimester screening the colour velocity scale should be about 50-70 cm/s for intracardiac structures and vessels, and lower, about 15-25 cm/s, for venous structures. Low colour persistence is ordinarily built into cardiac presets. Note: Approved by the editor on 13 Nov 2026 in an earlier wording (Dr Kunda Shahane, 2026-11-13 (approved review sheet for v0.2 in full; approval relayed by the project owner)). Reworded after the cross-check found: Color flow Doppler ultrasound, p. 796 recommends the two stated velocity scales. It describes low colour persistence as ordinarily built into cardiac presets, without giving it the same direct instruction as the scale setting. Needs the editor's re-approval.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Color flow Doppler ultrasound, p. 796D1, D2, D7, F1

AH14-313In D-transposition, a small or abnormal ductus with concerns about the foramen ovale indicates high risk of compromise and need for urgent balloon septostomy; such fetuses should be delivered where hypoxia and pulmonary hypertension can be managed. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Perinatal Management and Outcome of Fetuses With CHD, Foramen Ovale-Dependent Lesions, p. 2225Z3
AH14-315Planned cardioversion or antiarrhythmic therapy in the delivery room is indicated for uncontrolled tachycardia; planned chronotropic drugs or pacing in the early newborn period is reasonable for complete heart block. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Perinatal Management and Outcome of Fetuses With CHD, Fetal Arrhythmias, p. 2226Z3
AH14-317Level of care P: heart disease with palliative care planned (with a severe or fatal chromosomal or multisystem disease); arrange family support and palliative care; normal delivery at the local hospital. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 19 (level of care assignment), p. 2223Z3
AH14-318Level of care 1: heart disease without predicted instability in the delivery room or first days (for example VSD, AVSD, mild tetralogy); normal delivery at the local hospital with routine care and later cardiology review. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 19 (level of care assignment), p. 2223Z3
AH14-319Level of care 2: minimal risk of instability in the delivery room but needing catheterisation or surgery after birth (ductal-dependent lesions such as HLHS, critical coarctation, severe aortic stenosis, interrupted arch, PA/IVS, severe tetralogy); consider planned induction near term, delivery at a hospital with a neonatologist and accessible cardiology, start prostaglandin if indicated, then transfer. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 19 (level of care assignment), p. 2223Z3
AH14-320Level of care 3: likely instability in the delivery room needing immediate specialist stabilisation (d-TGA with concerning atrial septum primum - all d-TGA without an atrial septal defect may reasonably be considered at risk - uncontrolled arrhythmias, complete heart block with heart failure); planned induction at 38-39 weeks, caesarean if needed to coordinate, delivery where rapid stabilising care is possible, neonatologist and cardiac specialist in the delivery room. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 19 (level of care assignment), p. 2223Z3
AH14-321Level of care 4: expected instability at placental separation needing immediate catheterisation or surgery in the delivery room (HLHS with severely restrictive or intact atrial septum; d-TGA with severely restrictive or intact atrial septum and abnormal ductus; obstructed TAPVR; Ebstein with hydrops; tetralogy with absent pulmonary valve and severe airway obstruction; uncontrolled arrhythmia with hydrops; complete heart block with low ventricular rate, endocardial fibroelastosis or hydrops); caesarean in a cardiac facility with specialists in the delivery room, usually at 38-39 weeks. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 19 (level of care assignment), p. 2223Z3
AH14-322Level of care 5: heart disease for which transplantation is planned (HLHS with intact atrial septum, or heart disease including severe Ebstein or cardiomyopathy with severe ventricular dysfunction); listing after 35 weeks, caesarean when a heart is available, specialised cardiac team in the delivery room. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 19 (level of care assignment), p. 2223Z3
AH14-323For obstructed TAPVR, a decompressing vein below the diaphragm or accelerated flow in it should lead to consideration of ECMO (Class IIb, LOE C). Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 20 (fetal predictors for delivery planning), p. 2225Z3
AH14-324For complete heart block, a falling cardiovascular profile score (to below 7), very low ventricular rate, reduced function or endocardial fibroelastosis, or hydrops should lead to consideration of early delivery and of chronotropic drugs or temporary pacing in the delivery room (Class IIa, LOE C). Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 20 (fetal predictors for delivery planning), p. 2225Z3
AH14-325In d-TGA, foramen ovale findings reported to predict restriction are: septum primum angle below 30° to the atrial septum, bowing of septum primum more than 50% into the left atrium, loss of normal swinging motion, and a hypermobile septum primum; these call for planned urgent balloon atrial septostomy, on site if possible (Class I, LOE B), and prostaglandin E1 (I, B). Note: The table adds that all fetuses with d-TGA and a concerning septum primum should be considered at risk. Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 20 (fetal predictors for delivery planning), p. 2225Z3
AH14-327In tetralogy with absent pulmonary valve, lung findings of lobar emphysema (fluid trapping) on MRI suggest planning specialised ventilation and considering ECMO (Class IIb, LOE C). Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 20 (fetal predictors for delivery planning), p. 2225Z3
AH14-328In Ebstein anomaly with hydrops or uncontrolled arrhythmia, early delivery may be considered, with measures to lower pulmonary resistance, treat arrhythmia and support output (Class IIb, LOE C). Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 20 (fetal predictors for delivery planning), p. 2225Z3
AH14-329In tachyarrhythmia with rapid rate, reduced function, or pericardial effusion or hydrops, early delivery should be considered if gestation is appropriate, with urgent cardioversion or medical therapy in the delivery room if possible (Class I, LOE C). Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 20 (fetal predictors for delivery planning), p. 2225Z3
AS23-001Two-dimensional, spectral Doppler and colour Doppler modalities should all be used in a fetal echocardiogram, with imaging settings optimised specifically for the fetal heart.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Section III Key Points, p. 697; III.A Equipment, p. 683F1, XA5
AS23-002The ultrasound system used for fetal echocardiography needs, as a minimum, two-dimensional (B-mode), M-mode, colour flow and pulsed-wave Doppler capability.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.A Equipment, p. 683F1
AS23-003Where the system has it, continuous-wave Doppler can be used to characterise high flow velocities. Note: Reworded after the cross-check found: III.A, Equipment, p. 683 makes CW Doppler an option for characterising high velocities when available. The claim changes a permitted use to a categorical description.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.A Equipment, p. 683F1
AS23-004Curvilinear transducers are preferred; linear and sector transducers may also be used. A frequency range of 2 to 7 MHz is recommended for the late second and third trimesters; 5 to 12 MHz may help in the late first and early second trimesters. Note: Reworded after the cross-check found: III.A, Equipment, p. 683 recommends a 2–7 MHz range for late second- and third-trimester scanning. The 5–12 MHz range for the earlier window is a possible aid. The claim treats the first range as merely suitable.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.A Equipment, p. 683D2, D9, F1
AS23-005Fetal echocardiographic studies follow the 'as low as reasonably achievable' principle; operators should be aware of the thermal and mechanical indices and limit power output and exposure time. Note: Reworded after the cross-check found: III.B, Acoustic Bioeffects, p. 684 applies ALARA to fetal echocardiographic studies. It says operators should be aware of TI and MI and limit power and exposure time. “Every fetal study” broadens the scope beyond the examination discussed.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.B Safety, p. 684D2, F1
AS23-006In early gestation the thermal and mechanical indices should be kept at or below 1.0 and Doppler modalities used sparingly.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 8 (early gestation), p. 695-696D7, D9, F1
AS23-007Scanning frame rates above 30 to 40 Hz are recommended; rates of 80 to 100 Hz may be needed to capture important events at heart rates above 140 beats per minute, or for speckle tracking. Narrowing the sector and choosing an appropriate depth help achieve this. Note: Reworded after the cross-check found: III.D, Image Optimization, p. 684 gives the higher 80–100 Hz range for capturing important events at heart rates above 140 beats/min or for speckle tracking. “Faster” omits the stated threshold. The baseline frame rate and adjustment techniques agree.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.D Image optimization, p. 684D2, F1
AS23-008The study should include still images, moving clips and a structured report. A sweep from the abdomen at the level of the stomach to the upper mediastinum is required, together with both two-dimensional and colour clips of the individual views the guideline names, including both the three-vessel view and the three-vessel-and-trachea view. Note: Reworded after the cross-check found: III.A, Storage, p. 684 says the study should include stills, motion and a structured report. It requires an abdominal-stomach to upper-mediastinal sweep and both 2D and colour clips for the named individual views, including both 3VV and 3VT. The claim drops the mode requirements.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.A Storage, p. 684; III.E, p. 684-688D13, F1, XA5
AS23-009Colour Doppler shows whether flow is present and in which direction; it is used to look for valve stenosis and regurgitation, flow across the foramen ovale, the integrity of the septa and the patency of vessels.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E Standard views: four-chamber view, p. 687; LV outflow tract, p. 688; RV outflow, three-vessel-and-trachea, bicaval and short-axis views, p. 689; Table 3, p. 686D7, F1
AS23-010For colour Doppler the Nyquist limit is set to suit the velocities of interest, and colour gain and persistence are adjusted so that colour fills the chamber or vessel without hiding the grey-scale image.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.D Image optimization, p. 684; III.G, p. 689D7, F1
AS23-011Power Doppler displays the amplitude of the Doppler signal rather than the frequency shift; it helps to show small vessels, low-velocity flow such as in veins, and septal defects. Directional power Doppler adds the direction of flow.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.G Color and Power Doppler Ultrasound, p. 689; III.D Image Optimization, p. 684 (septal defects)D7, F1
AS23-012Pulsed-wave Doppler gives the flow profile and direction at a chosen site. The beam should run along the flow or at an angle of less than 20 degrees to it; a small sample gate reduces the chance of sampling more than one site. Note: Reworded after the cross-check found: III.G, PW Doppler Ultrasound, p. 689 specifies alignment along flow or an angle strictly below 20°, excluding 20°. A small gate reduces the chance of sampling multiple sites. It does not guarantee a single-site signal.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.G Doppler ultrasonography, p. 689F1
AS23-013Sites where pulsed-wave Doppler is required in a fetal echocardiogram: umbilical vein, ductus venosus, at least one pulmonary vein on each side, tricuspid and mitral inflow, aortic and pulmonary outflow, the distal ductus arteriosus and the umbilical artery.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 6, p. 693F1, XA5
AS23-014Table 6 marks these pulsed-wave sites optional: hepatic vein, superior and inferior venae cavae, a great-artery and arch row that names the transverse aortic segment and the isthmus, branch pulmonary arteries, middle cerebral artery, a combined left ventricular inflow and outflow recording for isovolumic relaxation time, and tissue Doppler at the lateral tricuspid and mitral annulus. Note: The guideline text (III.G PW Doppler, p. 689; Figure 10, p. 694) includes 'arches' generically in its minimum pulsed-wave assessment, while Table 6 (p. 693) marks the transverse aortic segment and isthmus optional and separately requires the distal ductus arteriosus at its aortic insertion. The guideline does not reconcile the two. Confirmed by the ChatGPT cross-check of 16 Nov 2026. Editor to decide how the course teaches this (question Q1).ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 6, p. 693F1, XA5
AS23-015Continuous-wave Doppler is not needed when the heart is normal. It is used to characterise high velocities and valve gradients and to estimate pressure from an atrioventricular valve regurgitant jet, with the beam aligned along the jet.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.G CW Doppler Ultrasound, p. 692; III.A Equipment, p. 683F1, XC1
AS23-016When the rhythm is irregular, or bradycardia or tachycardia is seen, the mechanism should be documented with M-mode, pulsed-wave Doppler or tissue Doppler, alone or in combination.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, Key Points, p. 699; tools introduced p. 697D8, F1, F2
AS23-017M-mode times atrial against ventricular contraction precisely; the cursor is placed through an atrial wall and the free wall of a ventricle together.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Figure 11F, p. 697; IV.A, p. 699D8, F1, F2
AS23-018Pulsed-wave Doppler times atrial against ventricular events by sampling two flows at once: superior vena cava with ascending aorta, mitral inflow with aortic outflow, or pulmonary artery with pulmonary vein.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A Rhythm; Figure 11, p. 697D8, F1, F2
AS23-019Pulsed-wave tissue Doppler at the lateral mitral or tricuspid annulus records myocardial velocities and time intervals and may help in assessing rhythm, including bradycardia.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A, p. 699; Figure 11D, p. 697; Table 9, p. 698F1, F2
AS23-020M-mode is among the tools for assessing systolic function: ventricular shortening fraction and annular plane excursion of the tricuspid and mitral valves.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 10, p. 701F1, XC1
AS23-021Three-dimensional imaging and spatiotemporal image correlation (STIC) can add anatomical and functional information, but STIC has not been validated for clinical use.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.I Alternative ultrasound modalities, p. 693F1
AS23-022Tissue Doppler and strain imaging are discussed together as ways of assessing myocardial mechanics; two-dimensional strain (speckle tracking) may detect subclinical dysfunction. Their application in pregnancy needs further investigation. Note: Reworded after the cross-check found: III.I, Alternative Ultrasound Modalities, p. 693 discusses tissue Doppler and strain jointly for assessing myocardial mechanics. It attributes detection of subclinical dysfunction specifically to 2D strain/speckle tracking. Their application in pregnancy needs further investigation.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.I Alternative ultrasound modalities, p. 693F1, XC1
AS23-024Pregestational diabetes is an indication for fetal echocardiography.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: II. Indications, Table 1, ASE column, p. 681D11
AS23-025Maternal autoimmune disease with SSA/SSB antibody positivity is an indication for fetal echocardiography.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: II. Indications, Table 1, ASE column, p. 681D11, F2
AS23-026A first-degree family history of congenital heart disease is an indication for fetal echocardiography.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: II. Indications, Table 1, ASE column, p. 681D11
AS23-027After in vitro fertilisation, fetal echocardiography may be considered despite a normal cardiac screen, taking local screening accuracy into account.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: II. Indications, Table 1, ASE column and referral footnote, p. 681D11
AS23-028Hydrops on fetal screening is an indication for fetal echocardiography.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: II. Indications, Table 1, ASE column, p. 681D11
AS23-029An extracardiac anomaly on fetal screening is an indication for fetal echocardiography.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: II. Indications, Table 1, ASE column, p. 681D11
AS23-030Monochorionic twins are an indication for fetal echocardiography.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: II. Indications, Table 1, ASE column, p. 681D11
AS23-031At a nuchal translucency of 3.0–3.4 mm, referral for fetal echocardiography may be considered. After a normal cardiac screen, the decision should account for local screening accuracy.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: II. Indications, Table 1, ASE column and referral footnote, p. 681D11
AS23-032A nuchal translucency of 3.5 mm or greater is an indication for fetal echocardiography.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: II. Indications, Table 1, ASE column, p. 681D11
AS23-033An isolated single umbilical artery does not itself indicate fetal echocardiography when the second-trimester cardiac screen is normal.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: II. Indications, Table 1, ASE column and table footnote, p. 681D11
AS23-034The optimal window for a comprehensive transabdominal fetal echocardiogram is 18–22 weeks.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.A. Timing of Examination, Equipment, and Image Storage, Timing, p. 682XA5
AS23-035An abnormal fetal heart is usually reassessed every 2–8 weeks until about 34–36 weeks, with the interval guided by the lesion and clinical concerns.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.A. Timing of Examination, Equipment, and Image Storage, Timing, p. 682XA5, Z2
AS23-036Near-term reassessment is targeted to findings that could change care immediately after birth.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.A. Timing of Examination, Equipment, and Image Storage, Timing, p. 682XA5, Z2
AS23-037A normal midtrimester fetal echocardiogram generally needs no follow-up unless there is concern for a progressive lesion.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.A. Timing of Examination, Equipment, and Image Storage, Timing, p. 682XA5, Z2
AS23-038When a progressive lesion is suspected despite a normal midtrimester echocardiogram, repeat assessment is recommended at intervals of up to 2–4 weeks.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.A. Timing of Examination, Equipment, and Image Storage, Timing, p. 682XA5, Z2
AS23-040If a standard view cannot be obtained, the study is complete only if all the cardiovascular structures are adequately seen by another approach or are anatomically absent.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.H. Complete Fetal Cardiac Assessment Using Segmental Analysis, p. 692XA5
AS23-042Two-dimensional imaging is required for visceral and atrial situs. Colour Doppler is optional for that determination.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Table 3, situs row, p. 686D3, XA5
AS23-043The cardiac axis must be assessed in two dimensions. Measuring the angle is optional.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Table 3, cardiac axis row, p. 686D4, XA5, XA6
AS23-044A complete study requires a measured cardiac-to-thoracic area ratio.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Table 3, cardiac size row, p. 686; III.F, Table 4, p. 690D4, XA5, XA6
AS23-046Systemic venous connections require assessment with both two-dimensional and colour Doppler imaging.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Table 3, systemic venous connections row, p. 686; III.H, Table 7, p. 695XA5
AS23-047The four-chamber assessment must show pulmonary venous connections from at least one vein on each side using two-dimensional and colour Doppler imaging.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Table 3, pulmonary venous connections row, p. 686; four-chamber view, p. 687D4, XA5
AS23-048Imaging further pulmonary veins from either lung is optional once the required connection from each side has been demonstrated.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Table 3, pulmonary venous connections row, p. 686; III.H, Table 7, p. 695XA5
AS23-049The atrioventricular connections require assessment on two-dimensional and colour images in the four-chamber view.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Table 3, atrioventricular connections row, p. 686; III.H, Table 7, p. 695XA5
AS23-050Both two-dimensional and colour images are required to assess the ventricular septum and locate any defect.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Table 3, ventricular septum row, p. 686; four-chamber view, p. 687D4, XA5
AS23-051Assessing relative ventricular size in two dimensions is required. Measuring maximum ventricular length and width is optional.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Table 3, ventricular morphology row, p. 686XA5
AS23-052The normal left ventricular outflow view shows the outflow below the aortic valve, the valve itself, the region above it and the ascending aorta.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, LV outflow tract, Figure 5, pp. 687–688D5, XA5
AS23-053The normal right ventricular outflow view shows the tract below the pulmonary valve, the valve and the proximal pulmonary trunk. Its bifurcation may enter this plane.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, RV outflow tract, pp. 688–689; Figure 6, p. 687D5, XA5
AS23-054The right and left pulmonary artery origins at the bifurcation require two-dimensional and colour imaging. Measuring their diameters is optional.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Table 3, proximal branch pulmonary arteries row, p. 686D5, XA5
AS23-055In the normal three-vessel view, the pulmonary trunk, ascending aorta and superior vena cava appear in that order from fetal left to right.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Three-vessel view, p. 689; Figure 6, p. 687XA5
AS23-056In the three-vessel view, abnormalities of vessel number, size, alignment or arrangement should be recorded.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Three-vessel view, p. 689D6, XA5
AS23-057In the normal three-vessel-and-trachea view the two arches join the descending aorta on the left of the trachea.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Three-vessel-and-trachea view, p. 689; Figure 6, p. 687D6, XA5
AS23-058Colour Doppler should demonstrate patency and flow direction in both arches in the three-vessel-and-trachea view.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Three-vessel-and-trachea view, p. 689D6, XA5
AS23-059The sagittal bicaval view establishes whether the inferior vena cava is continuous.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Bicaval view, p. 689; Figure 8A, p. 688D3, XA5
AS23-060The bicaval view shows whether the superior and inferior venae cavae lie on the same side.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Bicaval view, p. 689; Figure 8A, p. 688D3, XA5
AS23-061The parasagittal aortic arch view should establish continuity from ascending to descending aorta.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Long-axis view of the aortic arch, p. 689; Figure 8B, p. 688XA5
AS23-062The examiner should assess the ascending aorta, transverse arch and isthmus for hypoplasia.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Long-axis view of the aortic arch, p. 689XA5
AS23-063Measuring the ductus and the aortic isthmus is optional in the standard assessment of arch size and shape.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Table 3, aortic and ductal arch morphology row, p. 686XA5
AS23-064A sagittal plane just left of the fetal midline usually shows the long axis of the ductal arch.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Long-axis view of the ductal arch, p. 689; Figure 8C, p. 688XA5
AS23-065To assess ductal restriction, systolic and diastolic velocities at both the pulmonary and aortic ends should be evaluated using colour or spectral Doppler, or both.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Long-axis view of the ductal arch, p. 689XA5
AS23-066A high short-axis view shows the aortic valve face-on with the right ventricular outflow and pulmonary artery wrapping in front of it.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Short-axis views, p. 689; Figure 7A, p. 688XA5
AS23-067The low short-axis view can show muscular ventricular septal defects when colour Doppler is added.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: III.E. Standard Views and Imaging Planes, Short-axis views, p. 689; Figure 7B–C, p. 688XA5
AS23-071A sustained fetal rate below 120 beats/min is abnormal at any gestation.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A. Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, p. 699D8, F2
AS23-072ASE describes a sustained rate above 160–180 beats/min as abnormal at any gestation. Note: The rhythm section gives a range for the upper threshold and does not select a single cutoff.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A. Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, p. 699D8, F2
AS23-073Every fetal echocardiogram must document the fetal heart rate and rhythm.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A. Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, Key Points, p. 699D8, F2, XA5
AS23-074A premature atrial beat resets the atrial rhythm, producing an incomplete compensatory pause.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A. Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, Table 9, p. 698; Figure 16, p. 700F2
AS23-075With a premature ventricular beat, the interval between successive atrial beats is preserved.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A. Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, Table 9, p. 698F2
AS23-076Sinus tachycardia is typically regular with a long interval from ventricular to atrial contraction and a rate below 200 beats/min.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A. Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, Table 9, p. 698F2
AS23-077In the common pathway-mediated reentrant supraventricular tachycardia, atrial and ventricular beats pair one-to-one with a short interval from ventricle to atrium.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A. Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, Table 9, p. 698; Figure 14B, p. 699F2
AS23-078In supraventricular tachycardia, ASE advises against using paired mitral inflow and aortic outflow to time the atrium because the inflow waves fuse.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A. Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, Table 9, p. 698F2
AS23-079One-to-one tachycardia with a long interval from ventricle to atrium is seen in ectopic atrial tachycardia and permanent junctional reciprocating tachycardia.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A. Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, Table 9, p. 698F2
AS23-080Atrial flutter produces rapid sawtooth atrial motion on M-mode, often with only every second or third atrial beat reaching the ventricles. Note: The source describes conventional M-mode here. No separate recommendation for colour M-mode was identified in the guideline.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A. Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, Table 9, p. 698; Figure 14A, p. 699F2
AS23-081In ventricular tachycardia, M-mode or paired arterial and venous Doppler can show atrial contractions independent of the ventricular rhythm. Note: The same table row describes the ventricular rate as usually slower than the atrial rate. That wording is unclear in context and should be independently checked before teaching a rate relationship.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A. Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, Table 9, p. 698F2
AS23-083In complete heart block, atrial and ventricular contractions are independent, with a ventricular rate typically between 50 and 80 beats/min.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A. Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, Table 9, p. 698; Figure 15, p. 699F2
AS23-084Repeated blocked premature atrial contractions can mimic second- or third-degree atrioventricular block and must be distinguished from it.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A. Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, Table 9, p. 698; Figure 17, p. 700D8, F2
AS23-085When the pregnant patient carries anti-Ro/La antibodies, the fetal mechanical PR interval may be measured to assess atrioventricular conduction. Note: The guideline gives no general numerical normal range for the mechanical PR interval. The 100 ms in Figure 13 refers to isovolumic relaxation time.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A. Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, p. 699; Figure 13, p. 697F2
AS23-086Evidence is unclear that routine surveillance of anti-Ro/La-exposed fetuses reduces progression to higher-degree atrioventricular block.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.A. Rhythm Disturbances and Tools for Assessment, p. 699F2
AS23-087Every fetal echocardiogram must include a qualitative assessment of systolic and diastolic function.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.B. Assessment of Fetal Cardiac Functional Abnormalities, Key Points, p. 704XA5, XC1
AS23-088When findings raise concern about cardiac function or output, quantitative assessment should be performed.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.B. Assessment of Fetal Cardiac Functional Abnormalities, Key Points, p. 704XA5, XC1
AS23-090Atrioventricular valve regurgitation on Doppler may indicate systolic dysfunction.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: IV.B. Assessment of Fetal Cardiac Functional Abnormalities, Imaging Tools for Assessing Fetal Cardiac Function, p. 703XA5, XC1

AS23-606Fetal heart disease at risk of heart failure (examples: hypoplastic left heart with mitral regurgitation, tetralogy with absent pulmonary valve, Ebstein anomaly, atrioventricular septal defect with valve regurgitation, cardiac tumours) is followed every 2-4 weeks with comprehensive function assessment. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 15 (follow-up imaging for specific CHD diagnoses), p. 719Z2
AS23-607Fetal heart disease at risk of arrhythmia (examples: long-QT syndrome, congenitally corrected transposition, left atrial isomerism) is followed every 2-4 weeks with documentation of rate and rhythm. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 15 (follow-up imaging for specific CHD diagnoses), p. 719Z2
AS23-608An extracardiac anomaly at risk of hydrops (examples: CPAM, sacrococcygeal teratoma, twin-twin transfusion, arteriovenous malformation, TRAP sequence, fetal anaemia) is followed every 2-4 weeks with comprehensive function assessment. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 15 (follow-up imaging for specific CHD diagnoses), p. 719Z2
AS23-609A fetus at risk of cyanosis after birth (examples: transposition with intact septum or ventricular septal defect, double-outlet right ventricle with subpulmonary defect, tetralogy) is followed every 4-8 weeks and late in the third trimester, assessing atrial septal excursion, foramen opening and ductal shunting, with maternal hyperoxygenation testing considered. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 15 (follow-up imaging for specific CHD diagnoses), p. 719Z2
AS23-610A fetus at risk of pulmonary venous obstruction after birth (examples: hypoplastic left heart with restrictive atrial septum, obstructed anomalous pulmonary venous return, cor triatriatum) is followed every 4-8 weeks and late in the third trimester, assessing the pulmonary venous forward-to-reverse ratio, atrial septal position and thickness, vertical vein Doppler, with maternal hyperoxygenation testing considered. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 15 (follow-up imaging for specific CHD diagnoses), p. 719Z2
AS23-611Fetal tachycardia (atrial flutter, supraventricular tachycardia) is followed every 2 weeks unless well controlled, assessing rate and rhythm, heart size, hydrops and heart failure. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 15 (follow-up imaging for specific CHD diagnoses), p. 719Z2
AS23-612A fetus at risk of respiratory compromise after birth (examples: tetralogy with absent pulmonary valve, Ebstein anomaly, hypoplastic left heart with restrictive atrial septum) is followed every 4-8 weeks and late in the third trimester, assessing mediastinal shift, cardiothoracic area ratio and ventricular function, with fetal MRI of the lungs considered. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 15 (follow-up imaging for specific CHD diagnoses), p. 719Z2
AS23-613A fetus at risk of atrioventricular block (congenitally corrected transposition, left atrial isomerism, others) is followed every 2-4 weeks, assessing the atrioventricular interval, atrial and ventricular rates, hydrops and extracardiac Doppler. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 15 (follow-up imaging for specific CHD diagnoses), p. 719Z2
AS23-614After fetal intervention for aortic stenosis with evolving hypoplastic left heart, follow-up is every 4 weeks in the third trimester, assessing aortic outflow, arch flow direction, atrial septal flow, left ventricular size and function, mitral regurgitation and endocardial brightness. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 15 (follow-up imaging for specific CHD diagnoses), p. 719Z2, Z5
AS23-615After fetal intervention for hypoplastic left heart with restrictive atrial septum, follow-up is every 4 weeks in the third trimester, assessing patency of the atrial communication and the pulmonary venous forward-to-reverse ratio. Note: Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026.ASE-2023-FETALECHO: Table 15 (follow-up imaging for specific CHD diagnoses), p. 719Z2, Z5
IS23-001The guideline gives recommendations for cardiac screening of low-risk pregnancies in the second trimester, and also considers late first-trimester and early second-trimester screening where technically feasible.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Introduction, p. 788D0, D9
IS23-002The 2023 update encourages colour flow Doppler and adds new sections on quality assurance and on use of a checklist.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Introduction, p. 788; Appendix 1, p. 802D7, D13
IS23-005Variation in detection is partly explained by examiner ability, transducer frequency, body habitus, abdominal scars, gestational age, amniotic fluid volume and fetal position.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Introduction, p. 788D0, D2
IS23-006Continuous feedback-based training, a low threshold for echocardiography referral, standardised protocols and easy access to fetal heart specialists can improve the performance of a screening programme. Note: Reworded after the cross-check found: Introduction, p. 788 says the listed measures can improve programme performance. The claim states the performance benefit without that qualification.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Introduction, p. 788D0, D11, D13
IS23-011Screening at 20-22 weeks is less likely to need an additional scan for completion than screening at 18-20 weeks, although many patients prefer to know about major defects as early as possible.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Gestational age, p. 789D2
IS23-020The standardised workflow can also identify semilunar valve abnormalities such as aortic and pulmonary stenosis, which may progress in severity as pregnancy advances.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Cardiac examination, p. 789D0, D5
IS23-039The cardiac crux is the point where the lower atrial septum meets the upper ventricular septum and where the atrioventricular valves insert.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Four-chamber view, p. 792D4
IS23-041When colour Doppler is used to show the pulmonary veins entering the left atrium, it should be displayed alongside the B-mode image to avoid false-negative findings. Note: Reworded after the cross-check found: Four-chamber view, p. 792 advises displaying colour alongside B-mode in the passage about showing pulmonary veins entering the left atrium. The claim turns this into a rule for every use of colour Doppler.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Four-chamber view, p. 792D4, D7, F1
IS23-046Small septal defects (1-2 mm) can be very difficult to confirm; most are of limited clinical significance and may close spontaneously in utero.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Four-chamber view, p. 793D4, D10
IS23-048The left and right ventricular outflow-tract views and the three-vessel and three-vessel-and-trachea views are an integral part of the cardiac screening examination.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Outflow-tract, three-vessel and three-vessel-and-trachea views, p. 793D5, D13
IS23-049For the two great arteries, the examiner should establish connection to the correct ventricle, size, position relative to each other, and normal appearance and opening of the semilunar valves.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Outflow-tract, three-vessel and three-vessel-and-trachea views, p. 793D5
IS23-050In a survey of over 18 000 fetuses, 93% of examinations with an adequate four-chamber view also achieved satisfactory outflow-tract evaluation; non-visualisation rates were 4.2% for the left outflow tract, 1.6% for the right and 1.3% for both.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Outflow-tract, three-vessel and three-vessel-and-trachea views, p. 793D5
IS23-053The three-vessel and three-vessel-and-trachea views help detect anomalies of the outflow tracts, aortic arch and systemic veins, including persistent left superior vena cava, and thymic anomalies.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Outflow-tract, three-vessel and three-vessel-and-trachea views, p. 793D6
IS23-057Rotational technique: from the four-chamber view the transducer is rotated towards the fetal right shoulder; it is easier when the septum is perpendicular to the beam, may need slightly more skill, and optimises the LVOT, especially the outlet septum in continuity with the anterior aortic wall.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Outflow tracts: Sonographic technique, p. 793D5
IS23-058Once the LVOT is obtained, the transducer is angled cephalad until the pulmonary artery is seen running almost perpendicular to the aorta; the relationship of the two outflow tracts is best shown on cine clips, not still frames.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Outflow tracts: Sonographic technique, p. 793D5
IS23-061Sagittal views of the aortic and ductal arches and assessment of the neck vessels are not currently part of the routine cardiac screening examination.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: LVOT view, p. 794D5
IS23-070The aortic arch is more cranial than the ductal arch, so showing both together may need slight adjustment away from a true axial plane.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: RVOT view, 3VV and 3VTV, p. 796D6, D10
IS23-072Anomalies found on the three-vessel views can change counselling and management, for example prompting testing for 22q11 microdeletion, planning delivery location (as in complete transposition), anticipating prostaglandin infusion, or anticipating airway problems from vascular compression.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: RVOT view, 3VV and 3VTV, p. 796D6, D11
IS23-075Colour Doppler may be valuable in obese patients and may further improve detection of major heart disease in low-risk pregnancies.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Color flow Doppler ultrasound, p. 796D7
IS23-079With a significant risk factor for congenital heart disease, fetal echocardiography is indicated in addition to routine screening, depending on local resources, setting, examiner availability and screening results (good practice point).ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Fetal echocardiography, p. 796D11
IS23-081Nuchal translucency of 3.5 mm or more at 11-14 weeks is an indication for detailed cardiac evaluation even if the measurement later falls within the normal range.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Fetal echocardiography, p. 797D9, D11
IS23-082Common fetal indications for fetal echocardiography: suspected cardiac structural anomaly; extracardiac structural anomaly with a known association with congenital heart disease; suspected abnormal function or cardiomegaly; hydrops; persistent tachycardia (180 bpm or more); suspected heart block or persistent bradycardia (110 bpm or less); frequent or persistently irregular rhythm; nuchal translucency 3.5 mm or more; confirmed or suspected genetic abnormality; monochorionic twinning (if resources allow). Note: Reworded after the cross-check found: Table 2, Fetal factors, p. 797 specifies a suspected cardiac structural anomaly. An extracardiac structural anomaly is an indication here when it has a known association with CHD. The unqualified first item broadens referral.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Table 2, 'Fetal factors', p. 797D8, D11
IS23-083Common patient or familial indications: congenital heart disease in a first-degree relative of the fetus (parents, siblings and half-siblings); first- or second-degree relative with Mendelian disease and childhood cardiac manifestations; pregestational diabetes regardless of HbA1c; anti-Ro/SSA antibodies; phenylketonuria (unknown status or periconceptional phenylalanine above 10 mg/dL); retinoid exposure; confirmed fetal infection (TORCH or parvovirus B19). Note: Reworded after the cross-check found: Table 2, Patient or familial disease or environmental exposure, p. 797 explicitly includes parents, siblings and half-siblings in its first family-history entry. Reporting only the degree loses the table’s explicit inclusion of half-siblings.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Table 2, 'Patient or familial disease or environmental exposure', p. 797D11, F2
IS23-084Fetal echocardiography may be considered for: second-degree relative with congenital heart disease; gestational diabetes diagnosed in the first or early second trimester; nuchal translucency 3.0-3.4 mm; selected teratogens (for example paroxetine, carbamazepine, lithium, sodium valproate); conception by IVF including ICSI; use of ACE inhibitors.ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Table 2, 'Other indications when fetal echo may be considered', p. 797D9, D11
IS23-085Evidence is insufficient that the risk of congenital heart disease is significantly above baseline for: obesity (BMI 35 kg/m2 or more), SSRI exposure other than paroxetine, non-cardiac soft markers for aneuploidy, abnormal serum analytes, isolated single umbilical artery, gestational diabetes diagnosed after the second trimester, warfarin or alcohol exposure, echogenic intracardiac focus, prenatal fever or viral infection with seroconversion only, or isolated congenital heart disease in a relative more distant than second degree.
